privacy: Neutral content only; no secrets, tokens or personal data in Git. Component repositories are read, never written.
escalation: Material scope growth or effort increase goes to the owner before adoption
title: Shared assets section in docs/DOMAINS.md: bricks, blocks and the Gauntlet
goal: docs/DOMAINS.md gives the same three rules for each shared asset
acceptance: one Shared assets section covers bricks (UI: tokens, themes, components, genUI surfaces), blocks (shared domain logic, repository created with its first shared package) and the Gauntlet (model qualification)

for each: who owns what (the owning project, the shared repository, the consumer); for the Gauntlet, the owning project writes its domain cases (for example evals/gauntlet/<project>-v1.json), gauntlet-protocol provides runners, graders and general packs, NERV picks models per capability

for blocks the criterion is explicit: code imported by two or more projects; anything reached through MCP stays in its owning project; typed contract code (TypeScript types or validators for an MCP message format) imported by producer and consumer goes to a blocks contracts package, surface types stay in bricks, and a prose or JSON-schema contract stays under a Distributed contracts heading (NERV's MCP integration contract, such as the alert contract)
for each: new work checks the shared asset first and, when it is missing, proposes it there through the gap review, never a private copy
for each: a project that deliberately does not use it records a skip with its reason; bricks and blocks are recorded as not model-facing
the existing shared-code and screens rules are kept and linked, not restated

effort.basis: Estimated 2026-11-26 at agent speed for coordinator-only work; re-estimated the same day for the owner's widened scope. Not a measurement.
